verdict_line: Fundable at ₹30 crore, not ₹75 crore. The founder story and the human-in-the-loop design won the room; concentration risk and a founder-only sales engine cost the valuation.

fixes.title: Lead with the human-in-the-loop design
fixes.why: The RBI accountability answer flipped the toughest shark. It came in Round 2; it should be on slide 3.
fixes.how: Add one line under the solution slide: 'We never approve a loan. Every memo is signed by a human and carries a full audit trail.'

fixes.title: Kill the 41% concentration before the next raise
fixes.why: Two sharks named it as the number that keeps them up. It is the single biggest discount on your valuation.
fixes.how: Close the two signed January pilots and one new lender. Target: top customer under 30% of ARR within 12 months.

fixes.title: Replace the market comp with an earned valuation
fixes.why: 31x ARR from 'other rounds' read as fantasy. Founders who explain their number keep more equity.
fixes.how: Show net revenue retention, payback per lender and a 12-month ARR plan with named pipeline. Price off next-year ARR, not peers.

fixes.title: Turn sales into a machine, not a founder
fixes.why: A 4-6 month cycle with one seller pushed the brand shark out.
fixes.how: Productise a 30-day paid pilot with a fixed success metric (TAT and analyst hours saved), and hire one enterprise seller from an LOS vendor.

fixes.title: Name your moat as data, with a number
fixes.why: 'They are slow' did not convince the competition hawk. '11,400 labelled credit files' did.
fixes.how: Put the labelled-file count, its growth rate and the fraud-catch rate versus manual review on the competition slide.

objections.q: Thirty-one times revenue. How did you arrive at this number?
objections.weak: We looked at the last three lending-infra rounds.
objections.strong: We price off next year, not peers: [next-year ARR target] backed by the two signed January term sheets and a named pipeline of [N] lenders. Here is the pipeline, lender by lender.

objections.q: What if your biggest customer walks?
objections.strong: They are on a [contract term] contract with [notice period] notice, and our plan gets every lender under 30% of ARR within 12 months. Here is the plan, quarter by quarter.

objections.q: What happens when a bureau or LOS vendor gives this away free?
objections.weak: They are slow and want to sell big platforms.
objections.strong: Their free tool extracts data. Ours catches fraud with a model trained on 11,400 labelled credit files, at [catch rate]% above manual review. Bundling a spreadsheet does not bundle that.

objections.q: How do you sell, and how long does a deal take?
objections.weak: It's me, and it takes 4 to 6 months.
objections.strong: A 30-day paid pilot with one fixed success metric. Five of our six pilots have either paid or signed. With one enterprise seller we target a [target] week cycle.

pitch_v2: Every NBFC in India makes small businesses wait three days for a loan while analysts copy numbers from PDFs. CreditPilot reads bank statements, GST and bureau data in 90 seconds, catches fraud patterns using 11,400 labelled credit outcomes, and drafts a credit memo where every number links to its source. We never approve a loan: a human signs every memo, with a full audit trail built for RBI. Six lenders are live, three pay us, ARR is ₹2.4 crore at 78% gross margin, and two more have signed for January. We are raising ₹1.5 crore to finish our model-risk audit, hire our first enterprise seller, and get no lender above 30% of revenue within a year.
metrics_to_bring: Fraud catch rate vs manual review
Named pipeline with stage and expected ARR
dd_checklist: Signed customer contracts and notice periods
Data processing agreements and data residency
Security review reports from pilot lenders

next_steps.action: Move the human-in-the-loop line onto the solution slide and rehearse the new valuation answer.
Close both January pilots as paid and appoint the model-risk auditor.
Hire one enterprise seller and launch the 30-day paid pilot package.
